summary: Attacked part 1 of the Representation theory area: ReductiveGroupsPartII, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, the Tau Ceti roadmaps ReductiveGroups, RepresentationTheory, ClassicalGroups and RootSystems, with the eleven roadmaps of the other two parts read for what is planned twice across them. Three findings: ClassicalGroups names RootSystems as the owner of the abstract Weyl dimension and character formulas, which RootSystems' own scope boundary assigns to LieHighestWeight; two candidate Part II roadmaps are proposed for RootSystems in the same direction, with the consolidation instruction recorded in only one of the six records; and two of those Part II titles are not the exact prefix extensions section 15 requires. The prerequisite graph, the SchurWeyl and LieHighestWeight boundaries, and the ReductiveGroups/Part II overlap (which RS-31 already resolves) all held.
checked: Every stage of all six roadmaps, with its document: ReductiveGroupsPartII (7 stages), SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (11), tauceti ReductiveGroups (10), tauceti ClassicalGroups (7), tauceti RootSystems (6), and RepresentationTheory (0).

RepresentationTheory's zero stages, which looked like a gap and is not one: its document says 'this page is the index and the map of how they fit together', so it is the family index rather than a planning roadmap, and it correctly records the six consumers that depend on the family.

Prerequisites across the area: every `requires` entry of the six roadmaps' 41 stages resolves to a real atlas stage, none dangling; and the whole atlas requires-graph, 1962 stages and 3382 edges, is acyclic, so nothing in the area sits in a cycle.

The eleven roadmaps of the other two parts (AdoIwasawa, CharacterTheory, InductionRestriction, QuiverRepresentations, SchurWeyl, SemisimpleAlgebras, CompactGroups, LieGroups, LieHighestWeight, SpinRepresentations, ZigzagPreprojective), for mathematics planned twice across the parts. A term-overlap comparison of all 142 stages of the seventeen roadmaps raised exactly one candidate pair, between AdoIwasawa's PBW layer and LieHighestWeight's enveloping-algebra layer, both in other parts and both about the same shared vocabulary rather than the same target; nothing involving my six.

The boundaries in this area that most often duplicate, read in the sources rather than inferred. ClassicalGroups Layer 2 pins the symmetric-group boundary outright ('`../SchurWeyl` owns the group algebra ℂ[Sₐ], the Young symmetrizer c_λ, and Schur-Weyl duality; this roadmap owns the GLₙ-equivariant image Sᵘ V'), and Layer 4 pins the Schur polynomials ('owned by `../SchurWeyl`, which already builds them; this roadmap consumes them and does not re-define them, avoiding a second incompatible foundation'). Neither is duplication.

The one substantial overlap inside the area, between tauceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7 and ReductiveGroupsPartII: Layer 7 lists 'the relative root system for non-split groups' and 'Bruhat decomposition and BN-pairs / Tits systems' among its own targets, while RG2.1 constructs relative roots and a relative Weyl group and RG2.4 proves Cartan and Iwahori-Bruhat decompositions. Not reported, because RS-31 already resolves it: its owners move 'Underlying algebraic relative root system and relative Weyl group' and 'Abstract Bruhat decomposition and BN-pair/Tits-system theory' to anchor Layer 7, and it narrows RG2.1 and RG2.4 to import them, RG2.1's keeps beginning 'Import the algebraic relative roots and relative Weyl group of a maximal E-split torus ... from anchor Layer 7.'

Which restructuring proposals touch the area at all, so that a finding is not one somebody has already fixed: RS-05, RS-21, RS-24 and RS-31 name my roadmaps, and RS-17 names SchurWeyl. None of them names ClassicalGroups or RootSystems, which is why findings 1 to 3 stand unresolved.

The modulus character, which SR.2 uses ('normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character') and SR.6 uses ('its right adjoint is delta_P times the opposite-parabolic Jacquet functor') without any layer visibly constructing it. Not a gap: at the pin Mathlib has Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/ModularCharacter.lean with `modularCharacterFun` and `modularCharacter : G →* ℝ≥0`, together with `haarScalarFactor` in Haar/Unique.lean and the Haar/MulEquivHaarChar and Haar/DistribChar files.

Three further candidate omissions for the local-groups lane, each found already planned or already in the libraries: Moy-Prasad filtrations, which appear nowhere in the atlas by name but are exactly RG2.1's 'root subgroups and filtrations indexed by their actual valuation sets'; the Iwahori-Hecke algebra, which is SR.1's construction at U the Iwahori, since SR.1 'identif[ies] e_U corners with U-biinvariant Hecke algebras'; and the invariant measure behind SR.1's convolution, which SR.1 deliberately handles by A-valued volumes on open cosets and index denominators rather than by real-valued Haar measure.

ReductiveGroups Layer 8, the shortest layer in the area at 397 characters, covering the isomorphism and existence theorems, the classification of semisimple groups by Dynkin diagrams, central isogenies and Chevalley existence. Not reported: the layer is explicitly titled 'long horizon' and flags relative theory over a base and pseudo-reductive groups as 'far-future generalizations', so its thinness is a declared scope decision rather than an omission.

The papers routed to the area, by route: 34 to ReductiveGroupsPartII, 41 to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, 17 to tauceti ReductiveGroups, 6 to RootSystems and 2 to ClassicalGroups. ReductiveGroups carries nine distinct Part II candidates, which is not duplication because they run in nine distinct directions (monodromy models, Grothendieck-Serre, arithmetic models, coadjoint invariant theory, semiglobal flags, stabilizers and Levis, integral representations, modular representations of finite reductive groups, and sigma-dual homomorphisms). RootSystems' two candidates are finding 2.

findings.claim: ClassicalGroups names the wrong owner for the abstract Weyl dimension and character formulas. Layer 5 attributes the abstract Weyl dimension formula to the RootSystems roadmap, and Layer 4 attributes the general Weyl character formula to it as well. Both formulas are written with rho, and RootSystems' own scope boundary says in terms that rho and the rest of the weight-lattice apparatus are not built there and belong to LieHighestWeight. A worker building ClassicalGroups Layers 4-5 would look to RootSystems for an input it does not have and must not add.
findings.evidence: ClassicalGroups README, Layer 5, line 303: 'equivalently, the specialization of the abstract Weyl dimension formula `∏_{α > 0} ⟨λ + ρ, α⟩ / ⟨ρ, α⟩` from [`../RootSystems`](../RootSystems/README.md)'. Layer 4, lines 294-295: 'The general Weyl character formula for `SLₙ`, `Spₙ`, `SOₙ` follows from [`../RootSystems`](../RootSystems/README.md)'s Weyl-group sum over the appropriate root system.' Against RootSystems README, the 'Scope boundary' paragraph at lines 45-51: 'This roadmap stops at the root system, its Weyl group, chambers, and the classification. The weight and root lattices, the coweight and coroot lattices, the fundamental weights, dominant integral weights, and `ρ` - the lattice apparatus that the Weyl character and dimension formulas run on - are **not** built here; they belong to [the highest-weight roadmap](../LieHighestWeight/README.md)'. LieHighestWeight is the owner in fact as well as by that assignment: its Layer 6 is titled 'the Weyl character, dimension, and Kostant formulas' and states the dimension formula at line 524. No restructuring proposal resolves this: of RS-05, RS-17, RS-21, RS-24 and RS-31, the proposals that touch this area, none names ClassicalGroups or RootSystems. The accepted RootSystems link map does not cover it either; its overlap 2 records the same species of error at ClassicalGroups Layer 3 (a GL_n root datum named from RootSystems although GL_n is outside its scope) and its overlap 1 records the rho boundary between RootSystems and LieHighestWeight, but neither names ClassicalGroups Layer 4 or Layer 5.
findings.fix: In ClassicalGroups Layer 5, change the parenthesis to cite LieHighestWeight for the abstract Weyl dimension formula — ClassicalGroups already cites that roadmap ten times, including for the theorem of the highest weight — and keep RootSystems cited for what it does own, the positive system the product is indexed by. In Layer 4, split the sentence the same way: the Weyl-group sum is indexed by RootSystems' Weyl group and positive roots, while the character formula itself, which needs rho, comes from LieHighestWeight Layer 6. Neither change touches RootSystems, whose scope boundary is correct as written and should not be widened to absorb rho.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25.result.json, its part-ii route proposing the roadmap RootSystemsDominancePartII, against RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure as proposed by PAPER-HE-18, PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 and PAPER-ZHU-17
findings.claim: Two candidate Part II roadmaps are proposed for the same parent, this area's RootSystems, in the same direction. Five paper extractions route 21, 28, 22, 26 and 1 items to RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure, each saying it is reusing an existing candidate; PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 routes a further 8 items to a separate id, RootSystemsDominancePartII, and its record never mentions the older candidate. No coalescence entry in any of the six records links the two ids. Section 15 forbids planning the same direction twice, and the overlap is real rather than nominal: both are integral dominance for root systems.
findings.evidence: PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25's route: roadmap 'RootSystemsDominancePartII', parent 'tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems', 8 items, reason 'Extend the existing proposed owner for integral dominance by the reusable finite diagram-folding and invariant-step proof.' The string 'RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure' does not occur anywhere in that record, and its `coalescence` block is empty. The duplication is known to a later extraction but only there: PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 writes 'The Kisin–Zhou candidate RootSystemsDominancePartII overlaps this earlier direction: consolidate its dominant-coroot/Stembridge lane into this candidate at design intake, retaining both papers' stable item ids and the additional Frobenius-orbit proof obligation. Do not build two dominance orders.', and its `ownershipReconciliation` reads 'Retain RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure from HE21; consolidate the later KZ25 RootSystemsDominancePartII overlap at design intake.' That instruction travels with KPZ26's record only. A design job generated from PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25's own route would read a record that carries no cross-reference and no coalescence entry, and would build the second dominance order that KPZ26 says not to build. The four sibling extractions show the house practice KZ25 departs from: HE-18 'Reuse the RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure candidate from PAPER-HE-21 and PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26', ZHU-17 'Reuse the existing candidate identifier and shared supplier; this is an additional source, not a second roadmap.'
findings.fix: Consolidate onto RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure, the id five extractions share and the one PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 says to retain. Re-point PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25's part-ii route at that id, keeping its 8 item ids as KPZ26 asks, and record the identification where a design job will see it from either side: a coalescence entry in PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 naming RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure as the owner, and the reciprocal note in the retained candidate. If instead the maintainers judge the dominant-coroot/Stembridge lane to be a genuinely separate direction deserving its own roadmap, then KPZ26's 'Do not build two dominance orders' should be withdrawn in the same change, so that the two records do not give opposite instructions.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23.result.json and research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25.result.json, the `title` of their part-ii routes on this area's RootSystems roadmap
findings.claim: Two proposed Part II titles for this area's RootSystems roadmap are not the title section 15 requires. The rule is '<existing roadmap>, Part II: <what it adds>', and the parent's atlas title is 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification'. Both offending titles begin 'Root systems, Part II: ...', dropping the rest of the parent's title. One of them is worse than cosmetic: it gives a second, different title to the same roadmap id that four other extractions title correctly, so the atlas would carry one candidate roadmap under two names.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL section 15: the additions 'form a roadmap that extends the existing one, titled "<existing roadmap>, Part II: <what it adds>", with the existing roadmap as its first prerequisite.' The parent's atlas title is 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification'. PAPER-HE-18, PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 and PAPER-ZHU-17 all title the shared candidate 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: dominant subtraction and Demazure reduction', an exact prefix extension. PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 routes to that same id, RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure, under the title 'Root systems, Part II: dominance, affine orders and admissible pairs'. PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 titles its own candidate 'Root systems, Part II: integral dominance steps'. Neither is a prefix extension of the parent's atlas title.
findings.fix: Rewrite both titles as exact prefix extensions, keeping each one's own subtitle: PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23's becomes 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: dominance, affine orders and admissible pairs', and, if its route survives finding 2 as a separate roadmap, PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25's becomes 'Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: integral dominance steps'. If finding 2 is fixed by consolidation, PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23's title should simply be made identical to the four that already agree, since one roadmap id carries one title.
